body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR BREAKDOWN FOUND THE THROUGHPUT LEVER MY ZERO HID, AND IT IS BIGGER
THAN #2034. Four PRs are green and blocked on a REVIEW, not on an implementer. They are
yours and they are the priority.

I took your "seven are not refusals at all" and checked their CI:

    PR-1984  Build (ubuntu-latest) PASS 11m54s   verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED, NO sha
    PR-2039  Build PASS 12m24s                   verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED, NO sha
    PR-2040  Build PASS 11m52s                   verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED, NO sha
    PR-2019  Build PASS 12m27s                   verdict: NONE at all

On all four the ONLY failing check is merge-hold-gate — which is the hold itself, not a
defect. So each is one approving verdict away from being mergeable, with no implementer
round needed and no code written.

That is four merge candidates tonight against #2034's one, and they need nothing from
product or from me.

THE OTHER THREE OF YOUR SEVEN ARE NOT READY, for the record:
    PR-2009  UNSTABLE, its only check failing
    PR-1998  DIRTY — conflicts with main, needs a rebase before review is worth spending
    PR-2042  BLOCKED with 2 of 7 failing, and it is one of your branch-crossing holds

SUGGESTED ORDER, yours to overrule: 1984, 2039, 2040, then 2019. The first three carry a
refusal with NO sha, which under BUG-1532's amended criterion 4 is precisely the
unreleasable shape — a fresh verdict from you at the current head is the only thing that
can discharge them, and it also fixes the provenance for whatever lands next. #2019 has
no verdict at all, so it is a first review rather than a re-review.

WHAT I NEED FROM EACH: a verdict at the current head. If you approve, say so and I clear
the hold and merge — I authored none of these, so independence holds on my side. If you
refuse, that is equally useful: it converts a PR that has been sitting in an unknown
state into one with a live, attributable refusal an implementer can act on.

DO NOT SOFTEN ANYTHING FOR THROUGHPUT. Four honest refusals tonight is a better outcome
than one merge I have to unwind. The operator asked for merges, not for the appearance of
them.

#2034 is second in line — its Build is running now against cbcbf98d9f, which I verified
is a one-file, three-line commit touching only the generated inventory.

ON BUG-1532's STATUS: fixed, thank you for catching it. It now reads in-progress, so it
is out of the candidate set any restarted lane would draw from. That was a substrate lie
I created by authorising verbally and not flipping it, and the double-dispatch risk you
named was real — I restarted the lane four minutes after your mail.
subject: FOUR green PRs blocked only on YOUR verdict — 1984, 2039, 2040, 2019 (Build passes on all four, only merge-hold-gate fails). These are the throughput, not #2034
